output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency staffing. The move was described as like-for-like, but the import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included a 15-second hold-off for brief low-oxygen alarms, suppression of repeat notifications, and routing of probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. Pods A–C then went from about 38 to about 82 phone notifications per nurse per shift, and median acknowledgement time doubled from 34 s to 71 s. Pod D, which stayed on the old server, did not change. Bedside alarm volume was flat, so neither patient acuity nor the monitor update explains it. Incident rates rose equally for core, agency and new-graduate nurses, with the same agency share in Pod D, which had no rise. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Do not cap agency use or open performance reviews, because that would blame the wrong people. Do not switch off SpO2 forwarding either. Restore the full rule set, with clinical validation, and track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Then check the Room 14 reports of phones not ringing, and the sick-leave link, separately.
